sentences.text:
When Scooty of deceased reached in front of Pinnacle Apartment,
Near Ram Leela Ground and Bharat Petrol Pump, Indrapura, Ghaziabad, a bus bearing registration no. UP-14FT-6147 came with very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner being driven by respondent no.1/driver Vinod Kumar, hit the Scooty of deceased with a great force.
As a result of such impact, Scooty fell on the road and front of wheel of offending bus ran over head of the deceased due to which his head crushed.
Immediately deceased was taken to Shanti Gopal Nursing Home where his MLC was prepared and doctor declared him brought dead.
Post mortem
on the dead body of deceased was conducted on 04.12.2016.
Respondent no.2 is owner of the offending bus and it was insured with respondent no.3/ insurance company.
2. Upon issuance of notice of claim petition, respondents i.e. driver, owner as well as counsel for the insurance company of offending vehicle appeared.

3. A joint Written Statement to the claim petition DAR was filed on behalf of respondent no.1 and 2 wherein it is pleaded that no accident as alleged has taken place and police officials falsely implicated respondent no.1 and 2 to benefit the claimants.
It is stated that FIR was registered MACT No.280/2017 Page 2 against unknown vehicle and after one week vehicle of R2 has been falsely implicated in the FIR.
It is stated that deceased was driving his vehicle without driving licence.
It is stated that no documentary evidence has been filed to substantiate the claim and claim is exaggerated.
It is stated that R1 is having valid DL and vehicle of R2 is insured with R3 at the time of alleged incident.
4. In Written Statement filed by R3/insurance company, it is stated that no compensation claimed is highly exorbitant and without any basis.
It is stated that claimants are not entitled to any compensation as well as interest for the period of delay in filing medical documents or other documents.

It is stated that driver of the offending vehicle had no valid DL at the time of alleged accident but still R2 permitted him to drive the vehicle and committed breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy.
In alternative it is stated that deceased was driving his Scooty negligently and carelessly and himself was instrumental in getting hurt which resulted into his death.
Thus deceased himself was responsible for his tragic death and claimants cannot take advantage of negligent of their son.

It is stated that this Tribunal has no territorial jurisdiction inasmuch as accident has taken place in Ghaziabad and claimants/deceased are also residents of Ghaziabad.
5.

On the basis of pleadings of parties, ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal framed following issues on 31.10.2017 :
(1)Whether respondent no.1 was driving vehicle no. UP-14FT-6147 on 03.12.2016 at 6.00 pm in front of Pinnacle Apartments, near Ramleela Ground and Bharat Petrol Pum, Indrapura, Ghaziabad in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and hit against scooty bearing no. UP-14CF-5716 being driven by deceased Ayush Verma who sustained fatal injuries?
OPP MACT No.280/2017 Page 3 (2)Whether
the petitioners are entitled for any compensation, if so and for what amount?
OPP (3)Relief.

Issue No.1 8.
It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.

UP 14FT 6147 was being driven in a rash and negligent manner as well as in a very high speed, violating traffic rules, said bus hit the scooty of son of PW1 with great force.
As a result Scooty fell down on the road and front wheel of driver side of the bus crushed the head of the deceased.
PW1 further stated that his son was taken to Shanti Gopal Nursing Home, Indrapuram where doctor declared him to be brought dead.
PW1 further deposes regarding post mortem conducted at District Mortuary, Ghaziabad.

10. Eye witness to the accident PW3 Nakul Madan deposed that on 03.12.2016 he was returning to his house from 3G Mall Indrapuram on his motorcycle when he saw that bus bearing registration no. UP 14FT 6147 being driven by the driver at very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner came from the back and hit the scooty bearing no. UP 14CS 5716.
As a result of which scooty fell down and front left tyre of the bus ran over the head of the deceased.
11. Counsel for the insurance company/respondent no.3 submits that there is no sufficient evidence proving rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
However I find that the evidence of PW3 being eye witness to the accident is consistent and cogent.
Nothing came in his cross examination to disbelieve the version of accident as deposed by him.
Rather in cross-examination also PW3 specifically deposed that offending vehicle did not stop at the accident site and fled away after the accident.

PW3 further stated that his statement was recorded by the police, PW3 MACT No.280/2017 Page 5 stated to have informed the police about the registration number of offending Suman Verma vs Vinod Kumar And Ors on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147696126/

sentences.text: Thus from the evidence of PW3 it is very much clear that accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the offending bus bearing registration no. UP 14FT 6147 being driven by respondent no.1.
This fact gets corroboration from the fact that police also charge sheeted respondent no.1 in crime case no.1826/2016 of PS Indrapuram, District Ghaziabad registered regarding accident in question.
Petitioner/ PW1 in his evidence referred to certified copy of FIR, site plan of the accident, post mortem report of deceased, vehicle mechanical inspection report.
Mechanical inspection report of bus no. UP 14FT 6147 also established that the front bumper of the bus was damaged.
Similarly the scooty of the deceased was also damaged establishing that accident was caused due to impact of bumper of the bus on the rear side of the scooty.

12. Thus, the facts that FIR has been registered and criminal proceedings have been initiated against the respondent no.1 by the police, are sufficient proof to conclude that respondent no.1 was negligent.

Reference may be given to judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the case titled as Shabina v. Satvir & Ors. MAC. APP. 980/17 dated 24.01.2020, wherein it has been observed that in so far as FIR has been registered, criminal case has been initiated against driver of offending vehicle and vehicle was seized, the requirement of proving the preponderance of probability of accident having been caused by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle has been established.

On perusal of the award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced (i) certified copy of the criminal record of criminal case in FIR No. 955/2004, pertaining to involvement of the offending vehicle,
(ii) Criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of charge sheet under Section 279/304-A IPC against the driver, (iii) certified copy of FIR,
wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle of the deceased.
These documents are sufficient proofs to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.
Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

Hence,
this contention of the counsel of the appellant also falls face down.

There is ample evidence on record to prove negligence on the part of driver."
13.

Therefore, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioners.

sentences.text: In view of the finding on issue no.1, both petitioner i.e. parents of deceased are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

15. Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the MACT No.280/2017 Page 7 claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 16.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)

The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 MACT No.280/2017 Page 9 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.
The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."

sentences.text: The learned Tribunal has taken the notional income of the deceased as Rs.22,500/- per annum MACT No.280/2017 Page 13 i.e. Rs.1,875/- per month which is less than even the minimum wages of a daily wager.
The approach and finding of the learned Tribunal is absurd and without any basis.
The law in this regard is well settled by catena of judgments.

Where the deceased is educated or is pursuing the professional course

An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Issue No.1 8.
It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
9.
12. Thus, the facts that FIR has been registered and criminal proceedings have been initiated against the respondent no.1 by the police, are sufficient proof to conclude that respondent no.1 was negligent.
In view of the above, this Tribunal finds that there is sufficient material on record to establish that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing registration no.UP 14FT 6147 by respondent no.1 and that has resulted into fatal injuries to deceased.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, both petitioner i.e. parents of deceased are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
These issues to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at the loss of dependency are:
(i) additions/ deductions to be made for arriving at the income;
(ii) the deduction to be made towards the personal living expenses of the deceased;
and iii) the multiplier to be applied with reference to the MACT No.280/2017 Page 8 age of the deceased.
If these determinations are standardized, there will be uniformity and consistency in the decisions.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.
Suman Verma vs Vinod Kumar And Ors on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147696126/
5 19.
To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
In Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Deo Patodi (2009) 13 SCC 123, the accident dated 12th June, 2003 resulted in MACT No.280/2017 Page 12 the death of a 22 year old brilliant student who had completed Business Administration Course and had an offer of job from a US based company at the time of the accident.
Reference in this regard may be made to judgment of Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. v. Deo Patudi, 2009 (8) Scale 194, in which case the deceased aged 22 years was a student having a brilliant career and offer of employment from a US Based Company at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30,
